topic: Research: xAI Grok Speech API Guide: STT and TTS for Developers (2026)
keyword: xAI Grok speech API STT TTS

key_points: Official April 17, 2026 launch post for standalone Grok Speech to Text and Text to Speech APIs.
Positions STT for large-file REST transcription and low-latency WebSocket streaming; highlights word-level timestamps, speaker diarization, multichannel support, and inverse text normalization.
Provides benchmark table claiming Grok STT overall word error rate of 6.9% versus ElevenLabs 9.0%, Deepgram 11.0%, and AssemblyAI 12.9%.
Lists STT pricing at $0.10 per hour for batch and $0.20 per hour for streaming; lists TTS pricing at $15.00 per 1 million characters.
Frames use cases as voice agents, real-time transcription tools, accessibility, podcasts, and interactive audio experiences.
Official implementation guide for POST https://api.x.ai/v1/stt and real-time WebSocket transcription.
Shows multipart file upload parameters including format, language, keyterm, and file.
Documents URL-based transcription, max 500 MB file input, raw audio hints, multichannel settings, diarize=true, filler word handling, and streaming query parameters.
Useful competitor SERP pattern: readers need copy-paste Python, JavaScript, and curl snippets, not just launch summaries.
Official implementation guide for POST https://api.x.ai/v1/tts and WebSocket TTS streaming.
Documents five built-in voices: eve, ara, rex, sal, and leo, with distinct tone guidance for demos, support, business, balanced narration, and instructional content.
Documents max 15,000 characters per REST request, language as BCP-47 code or auto, speech tags, custom voice IDs, voice listing endpoint, output_format, speed, and timestamp output.
Explains output codecs: MP3, WAV, PCM, mu-law, and A-law, with MP3 defaulting to 24 kHz / 128 kbps.
Developer-facing article focused on Grok STT endpoint, pricing, streaming, and the decision of when to use STT versus Voice Agent API versus TTS.
Ranks practical choices: REST for existing files, WebSocket for live audio, Voice Agent API only when the two-way spoken conversation is the product.
Includes concise contract details that searchers likely want: model id, endpoint, REST price, streaming price, region, rate limits, and common FAQ confusion between Grok and Groq.
Gap to beat: it focuses mostly on STT, so a stronger article should cover both STT and TTS plus full voice-agent architecture.
Shows an alternative access layer for xAI TTS and STT through Puter.js, with simple JavaScript examples.
Highlights the same reader benefits: five expressive voices, speech tags, diarization, word-level timestamps, and multichannel support.
Gives concrete browser-style examples for txt2speech and speech2txt, useful as inspiration for a 'front-end demo' section.
Gap to beat: does not cover direct xAI API production concerns such as keys, server-side proxying, rate limits, cost controls, or WebSocket handling.
News-style competitor targeting enterprise voice developers.
Summarizes STT features: batch and real-time transcription, 25 languages, 12 audio formats, diarization, word-level timestamps, inverse text normalization, and low hourly pricing.
Summarizes TTS features: five voices, speech tags, REST and WebSocket paths, and developer use cases such as voice assistants, IVR, accessibility, and podcast generation.
Contains at least one outdated/conflicting price claim for TTS ($4.20 per 1M chars), so the article should explicitly use current xAI docs and note that launch-era third-party posts may be stale.

stats.fact: xAI announced standalone Grok Speech to Text and Text to Speech APIs on April 17, 2026.
xAI release notes list Speech to Text general availability on April 15, 2026 and Text-to-Speech general availability on March 16, 2026.
Grok STT public model docs list REST pricing at $0.10/hour and streaming pricing at $0.20/hour.
Grok STT public model docs list rate limits of 600 RPM and 10 RPS for REST and streaming, plus 100 concurrent streaming sessions per team.
Grok STT public model docs list availability in the us-east-1 cluster.
Grok STT supports REST and streaming transcription, multiple audio formats, multiple languages, interim streaming results, keyterm prompting, and Smart Turn end-of-turn detection.
The xAI STT implementation guide says audio file uploads can be up to 500 MB.
xAI's launch benchmark reports overall WER of 6.9% for Grok STT, compared with 9.0% for ElevenLabs, 11.0% for Deepgram, and 12.9% for AssemblyAI.
xAI's launch benchmark reports Grok STT WER of 5.0% on phone call entities, 2.4% on video/podcasts, 10.9% on meetings, and 9.3% on telephone audio.
Grok TTS public model docs list pricing at $15.00 per 1 million characters.
Grok TTS public model docs list rate limits of 3,000 RPM, 50 RPS, and 100 concurrent sessions per team.
Grok TTS supports batch and streaming output, multiple voices, and MP3, WAV, PCM, mu-law, and A-law formats.
The xAI TTS implementation guide lists five voices: eve, ara, rex, sal, and leo.
The xAI TTS implementation guide says REST TTS text input is limited to 15,000 characters per request.
xAI release notes list Custom Voices on May 1, 2026, allowing cloned voices across TTS and Voice Agent APIs.

angles: Lead with the 2026 developer decision: use STT for audio-to-text, TTS for text-to-audio, and Voice Agent API only for full duplex speech-to-speech agents.
Make the article more useful than launch coverage by including REST and WebSocket architecture patterns, API key safety, retry/cost controls, and production checklist items.
Call out stale third-party pricing: several early posts mention lower TTS pricing, but current xAI docs and launch page show $15.00 per 1M characters.
Frame Grok STT's differentiator as business audio normalization: entity recognition, inverse text normalization, diarization, and multichannel support for calls and meetings.
Frame Grok TTS's differentiator as expressive delivery: five built-in voices, speech tags, streaming, telephony codecs, custom voices, and character timestamps.
Add a cost calculator section: batch STT hours, streaming STT hours, TTS character volume, and Voice Agent API hours are separate meters.
Include a 'Grok vs Groq' warning because searchers may confuse xAI Grok voice APIs with GroqCloud speech-related offerings.
Offer implementation recipes: file transcription, live captions, support-call diarization, podcast/read-aloud generation, IVR output, and cascaded STT -> LLM -> TTS agent.
Use benchmark claims carefully: attribute WER numbers to xAI's own launch benchmark and advise teams to test with their own accents, channels, domains, and noise.
